core.title: Order and number the steps of a wagon procedure
core.given: A document contains a wagon procedure written as steps
core.when: the step list is written, or any step is added, removed, moved, renumbered or edited
core.then: Steps are in an explicit order and each step carries a number.
prefer: After any edit, including numbering-only edits, re-check that every step still has a number and the order is unambiguous.
avoid: Unnumbered or unordered steps whose execution order a reader must guess.
core.why: Ordered, numbered steps with pre-conditions and outputs make a wagon procedure reproducible and checkable.
evidence: Reviewer confirms the steps are in an explicit order.
Reviewer confirms each step carries a number.
verification: Checked by review: severity 2, disposition documentation-only; the source defines no automated detector.
Term 'step' means a numbered unit of a wagon procedure.
The check covers only that an explicit order and a number on each step are present; it does not require consecutive numbering, positional numbering or any particular numbering format.

Scope split of the source statement 'Steps are ordered and numbered, and each declares its pre-conditions and its outputs': this rule covers the ordered-and-numbered half and requires the sibling obligation that each step declares its pre-conditions and outputs. That declaration obligation is carried by the sibling rule on step input/output declarations; the sibling's concrete rule id is a realization detail.

fires: A new wagon procedure is written as steps.
A step is added, removed or moved.
Step numbers are edited or deleted.
A step's content, pre-conditions or outputs are edited.
doesNotFire: Editing text that contains no wagon procedure steps.
Changing code with no change to any wagon procedure.

bunOnly.text: The declarations half is in planner.steps.sequence.declares-io.
bunOnly.reason: Only the concrete sibling-rule identifier is realization-specific: it binds this rule to the declarations rule under the Bun sidecar's legacy dotted id scheme. The dependency itself — that this rule requires the sibling obligation to declare each step's pre-conditions and outputs — is stack-neutral and is stated in core verification.

neutralityNotes: This convention governs document content (a wagon procedure's step list), not code, so nearly all of bun.json is already stack-neutral and is carried verbatim; 'wagon' is ATDD domain vocabulary (a bounded slice of the product), not a stack term. The core needs nothing from the structure profile: the rule deliberately applies to any document containing a wagon procedure, with no path, suffix or role restriction, so profileRequirements is empty. The activation facts' 'note' fields cannot be represented in the core fact schema (fact/values/observability only); their content is either captured by the observability value or remains in bun.json. The scope-split dependency — that this rule requires the sibling obligation for each step to declare its pre-conditions and outputs — is stack-neutral and is stated in core verification; only the concrete sibling-rule identifier 'planner.steps.sequence.declares-io' (the Bun sidecar's legacy dotted id scheme) is recorded as bunOnly. activation.fires and activation.doesNotFire are carried verbatim into the core and classified for completeness.
